data.title: Eddie Lazer, Head of Engineering at a16z Crypto, a
data.content:
## Summary
Eddie Lazer, Head of Engineering at a16z Crypto, argues that token design is fundamentally protocol design, where tokens act as tools to achieve specific decentralized goals. He outlines a structured framework for development—moving from goals and constraints to mechanisms—and provides a comprehensive taxonomy of token capabilities across five key categories.

## Key Points
- Tokens are tools that serve protocols, not the primary object of design.
- The protocol design process should flow from defining a measurable Goal to identifying Constraints, and finally selecting Mechanisms.
- Constraints are divided into endogenous (chosen trade-offs) and exogenous (imposed by tech or regulation).
- Common failure patterns include 'token-first thinking' and using the community as a 'wastebasket' for unresolved design problems.
- Token capabilities are categorized into five groups: Payment, Voting, Stakeholding, Metadata, and Claiming.
- Advanced token metadata can include embedded interfaces (HTML/JS) so the token carries its own UI.
